speaker: Doctor
text: I'm Dr. Agent, and I see you're experiencing agitation along with yellowing of your skin and eyes. To understand what's causing this, have you been feeling unusually fatigued or nauseous recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history; given your age, recent stimulant use, high-risk sexual behaviors, and new onset jaundice with agitation, I need to rule out acute liver failure and infectious etiologies. Have you experienced any abdominal pain, fever, or dark urine recently? REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Tests (LFTs), CBC, Coagulation Panel (PT/INR), HIV Ag/Ab, Hepatitis A/B/C serology, and CMV/EBV PCR.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 16.3 g/dL, Hematocrit: 47%, Leukocyte_Count: 9,750/mm3, Neutrophils: 58%, Bands: 2%, Eosinophils: 1%, Basophils: 0%, Lymphocytes: 24%, Monocytes: 2%, Platelet_Count: 365,000/mm3, Bilirubin: 25 mg/dL (elevated), AST: 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT: 650 IU/L (elevated), TP_Activity: < 40% (reduced), INR: 1.5 (elevated)

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Patient
text: The patient shows signs of psychomotor agitation and confusion. No other symptoms provided. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: I must clarify that acute appendicitis does not cause yellowing of the skin and eyes or these specific lab abnormalities; that presentation is highly atypical for appendicitis. Given your history of cocaine use and high-risk sexual behavior, the combination of agitation, jaundice, and confusion strongly suggests acute liver failure or a severe viral infection. Please tell me immediately if you have experienced any fever, dark urine, or bleeding gums recently. REQUEST TEST: Complete Liver Function Panel, Coagulation Profile (PT/INR), and Toxicology Screen.
